units: All *Px values are in the 1080x1920 design space (PSD FontSize * transform scaleY). anchor.x/baselineY are the PSD type origin: x is the alignment anchor, baselineY the first line's baseline.
notes: Every readable string on this invite is live HTML text. Nothing here may be shipped as flattened image type.

ALWAYS typeset a run at renderSizePx and raise it renderRaisePx above the line's baseline. sizePx/baselineShiftPx are the raw PSD numbers kept for traceability; for superscripts they are NOT what Photoshop drew. renderSizePx = sizePx * superscriptFactors.size (0.583) and renderRaisePx = baselineShiftPx + superscriptFactors.position (0.333) * sizePx. Never add a CSS vertical-align:super on top -- that would scale the glyph twice.

The four event-scene date-day superscripts verify against the client JPGs to under half a pixel under that model. The two cover "th" runs do not: their geometrySource is "measured:qa/textref" and the numbers came off qa/textref/cover.jpg. Do not recompute them from sizePx.

run.fontFeatures must be applied via font-feature-settings. All-caps runs carry "case", which is what gives Cormorant its tall lining figures -- without it "NOVEMBER, 2026" renders with short old-style figures. text-transform alone is not enough.

textTransform mirrors Photoshop's All Caps button. `text`/`lines` keep the designer's source casing ("Hari Family", "November, 2026") so the copy stays editable; `displayText` is what must appear on screen. Apply it with CSS text-transform, never by uppercasing the HTML source.

Rungkut's lowercase slots hold SMALL-CAP letterforms -- "Muskan" renders as a swashed M followed by small caps. Never text-transform:uppercase a Rungkut string; type the source casing exactly as it is in `text`.
run.ligatures is Photoshop's Ligatures checkbox -- it is OFF on every cover block, so those need font-variant-ligatures:none.

run.fauxBold is Photoshop's synthetic bold. The supplied families ship a single weight each, so it has to be emulated. It thickens the outline AND widens every advance by about 0.027em -- measured against the client JPGs: cover/venue line 1 renders 429px unstyled vs 458px in the reference (23 gaps -> 0.0275em), last/rsvp 176 vs 181 (0.025em), names/bride-name 327 vs 338 (0.029em). -webkit-text-stroke alone will NOT close the gap because it does not touch advances; pair it with a matching letter-spacing bump and re-measure against qa/textref.

block.outline is the layer's Photoshop Stroke effect -- the other thing that adds weight without touching advances, and the reason the cover's "Muskan & Shourya" is heavier than the same face elsewhere. Apply outline.webkitTextStrokePx as -webkit-text-stroke (already doubled for Photoshop's OUTSIDE position, and already in design px: Photoshop does not scale the effect with the layer's transform). It is null on every layer that carries no Stroke.
anchor.x is the PSD type origin (the centre for textAlign:center); bboxCenterX differs on the script faces because their swashes overhang asymmetrically -- trust anchor.x, use bbox only for QA.
